items.description: Analyze repository structure and document existing tooling
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/repo_analysis.md listing all modules (.archivara/, .opencode/, figures/, results/), their purposes, inter-module dependencies, and available agent capabilities (orchestrator, researcher, writer, reviewer, concept_worker). File must be >500 words.
items.notes: Completed: repo_analysis.md (1175 words) covers all modules, dependencies, agent capabilities. ConceptEvolve kickoff done with 12 concepts, 22 walk paths. Steering notes written with 3 prioritized directions.

items.description: Literature review: N-body gravity simulation methods
items.acceptance_criteria: Use web search to find and review at least 10 relevant papers and repositories covering: Newtonian N-body simulation, numerical integration schemes (Euler, Verlet, leapfrog, RK4, symplectic integrators), Barnes-Hut tree algorithm, fast multipole method. Create sources.bib in repo root with valid BibTeX entries for all consulted sources. At least 10 entries required.
items.notes: Completed: sources.bib with 16 entries covering N-body methods (Aarseth, Barnes-Hut, FMM), integration schemes (Verlet, Gladman, Marsden, Omelyan, Chambers, Skeel), modern codes (Abacus, heyoka), and reference texts (Binney & Tremaine).

items.description: Literature review: Real-time physics visualization and interactive simulations
items.acceptance_criteria: Search for state-of-the-art approaches to real-time gravity visualization (WebGL, Canvas 2D, Three.js, Pygame, etc.). Add at least 5 additional BibTeX entries to sources.bib covering visualization and interactive simulation techniques. Document findings in results/concept_evolve/tree/lit_review_visualization.md.
items.notes: Completed: lit_review_visualization.md written. 6 additional BibTeX entries added (hunter2007, waskom2021, springel2005, kratochvil2004, turk2011, mocz2020). Total sources.bib entries: 22.

items.description: Concept-tree exploration: Cross-domain reframing of gravity simulation
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve reframe on 'minimal gravity simulation' to generate at least 8 cross-domain analogies (e.g., molecular dynamics, crowd simulation, orbital mechanics, fluid particles). Output must exist in results/concept_evolve/tree/ with at least one concept card per domain. Document top 3 transferable ideas in results/concept_evolve/tree/cross_domain_insights.md.
items.notes: Completed: 10 reframings generated across 10 domains. cross_domain_insights.md documents top 3 transferable ideas: near-field/far-field decomposition, symplectic structure, softening/regularization.

items.description: Define scope and requirements for minimal gravity simulator
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/requirements.md specifying: target language/platform, minimum particle count (at least 100), required features (gravitational attraction, collision detection, visualization), performance targets (>30 FPS for 100 bodies), integration method candidates ranked by complexity vs accuracy trade-off. Must cite at least 3 papers from sources.bib.
items.notes: Completed: requirements.md with target language (Python), particle counts (100-2000), 7 feature categories, performance targets, integration method ranking citing 5 papers.

items.description: Implement naive O(N^2) pairwise gravity simulation with Euler integration
items.acceptance_criteria: Working Python script (src/gravity_sim.py) that: (1) simulates N gravitational bodies with configurable N>=100, (2) uses direct O(N^2) pairwise force computation, (3) uses forward Euler integration, (4) outputs position data per timestep to results/baseline/. Script runs without errors and produces at least 1000 timesteps of simulation data for N=50.
items.notes: Completed: src/gravity_sim.py with vectorized O(N^2) forces, Euler/Verlet/Leapfrog integrators, energy tracking, collision detection. Baseline run: N=50, 1000 steps, 0.15ms/step, 115.8% energy drift (expected for Euler).

items.description: Implement energy conservation metric
items.acceptance_criteria: Add total energy computation (kinetic + gravitational potential) to the simulation. Log energy at each timestep. Produce results/baseline/energy_drift.csv with columns [timestep, total_energy, kinetic_energy, potential_energy]. For the Euler baseline with N=50 over 1000 steps, report the relative energy drift percentage.
items.notes: Completed: Energy tracking built into gravity_sim.py (compute_total_energy, compute_kinetic_energy, compute_potential_energy_vectorized). results/baseline/energy_drift.csv produced with 1001 rows. Euler N=50 energy drift: 115.83% over 1000 steps.

items.description: Implement basic 2D visualization
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/visualize.py that renders body positions as a 2D scatter plot animation. Must support: (1) reading simulation output from results/, (2) generating either a live animation window or saved GIF/MP4 in figures/. At least one visualization artifact must exist in figures/ after running.
items.notes: Completed: src/visualize.py with animation (GIF), static snapshots, and energy drift plots. 5 artifacts in figures/.

items.description: Establish performance benchmarks for baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Measure and record wall-clock time per timestep for N in {10, 50, 100, 200, 500}. Store results in results/baseline/performance.csv with columns [N, time_per_step_ms, total_time_s]. Verify O(N^2) scaling by plotting N vs time_per_step in figures/baseline_scaling.png. Fit a polynomial and confirm exponent is approximately 2.0 (between 1.8 and 2.2).
items.notes: Completed: performance.csv for N={10,50,100,200,300,400,500}. Scaling exponent: 2.09 (within 1.8-2.2 range). baseline_scaling.png generated.

items.description: Implement test suite for physics correctness
items.acceptance_criteria: Create tests/test_physics.py with at least 5 unit tests: (1) two-body Keplerian orbit period within 5% of analytical solution, (2) momentum conservation within 1e-10, (3) energy computation correctness against hand-calculated values, (4) force symmetry (F_ij = -F_ji), (5) zero-force for single body. All tests pass.
items.notes: Completed: 13 tests all passing. Covers force symmetry, zero force, energy computation, momentum conservation, Keplerian orbit period, leapfrog energy bounds.

items.description: Implement Velocity Verlet (Stormer-Verlet) integrator
items.acceptance_criteria: Add Velocity Verlet integration to src/gravity_sim.py as a selectable method. Run the same N=50, 1000-step scenario as baseline. Energy drift must be at least 10x smaller than forward Euler. Store results in results/verlet/ with same CSV format as baseline.
items.notes: Compare against symplectic integrator papers cited in sources.bib.

items.description: Implement leapfrog (kick-drift-kick) symplectic integrator
items.acceptance_criteria: Add leapfrog integration as a third selectable method. Demonstrate bounded energy oscillation (no secular drift) over 10000 timesteps for N=50. Produce results/leapfrog/energy_drift.csv showing energy remains within 0.1% of initial value. Compare quantitatively against Euler and Verlet in results/integrator_comparison.csv.

items.description: Implement Barnes-Hut tree-based force approximation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create src/barneshut.py implementing the Barnes-Hut octree (or quadtree for 2D) algorithm with configurable theta parameter. For theta=0.5, force accuracy must be within 5% of direct summation for 95% of bodies. Must reduce time complexity demonstrably: for N=500, Barnes-Hut must be at least 2x faster than direct O(N^2). Store timing results in results/barneshut/performance.csv.

items.description: Concept-tree exploration: Novel optimization strategies
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve evolve on 'gravity simulation performance optimization' to explore cross-domain optimization strategies (GPU parallelism, spatial hashing, adaptive timestep, etc.). Produce at least 3 concept cards in results/concept_evolve/tree/ with actionable optimization ideas. Select and document the most promising approach in results/concept_evolve/tree/optimization_selection.md with justification referencing at least 2 papers from sources.bib.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer must traverse the generated tree and identify highest-value paths.

items.description: Implement adaptive timestep control
items.acceptance_criteria: Add adaptive timestep to the simulation based on closest-approach distance or maximum acceleration. Must maintain energy conservation within 0.5% over 10000 steps while using at least 30% fewer total force evaluations than fixed timestep for the same physical duration. Document the adaptive criterion and comparison in results/adaptive/comparison.md.

items.description: Implement collision detection and response
items.acceptance_criteria: Add elastic or inelastic collision handling (configurable). Bodies that overlap within a softening radius merge or bounce. Test with a scenario of 20 bodies in a confined region where collisions are guaranteed within 500 timesteps. Produce results/collisions/collision_log.csv recording each collision event (timestep, body_i, body_j, type). At least 5 collision events recorded.

items.description: Comparative experiment: integrator accuracy vs performance
items.acceptance_criteria: Run all three integrators (Euler, Verlet, Leapfrog) on identical initial conditions (N=100, 5000 steps, random seed 42) with 5 different timestep sizes (dt in {0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1}). Produce results/experiments/integrator_accuracy.csv with columns [integrator, dt, final_energy_drift_pct, wall_time_s, momentum_drift]. Generate figures/integrator_comparison.png showing energy drift vs dt for all three methods. Cite and compare against theoretical convergence orders from literature.

items.description: Scaling experiment: direct vs Barnes-Hut
items.acceptance_criteria: Benchmark direct O(N^2) vs Barnes-Hut for N in {50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000}. Produce results/experiments/scaling.csv with columns [method, N, theta, time_per_step_ms]. Generate figures/scaling_comparison.png with log-log plot showing O(N^2) vs O(N log N) scaling. Barnes-Hut crossover point (where it becomes faster) must be identified and documented.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: use concept-tree-explorer to analyze scaling results and propose next experiments.

items.description: Physical scenario: solar system model
items.acceptance_criteria: Create scenarios/solar_system.json with real mass ratios and orbital radii for Sun + 4 inner planets. Simulate for at least 1 Earth-year equivalent with leapfrog integrator. Verify orbital periods match known values within 10%. Produce figures/solar_system_orbits.png showing orbital traces. Document deviations in results/experiments/solar_system_validation.md.

items.description: Physical scenario: gravitational collapse of random cloud
items.acceptance_criteria: Initialize N=200 bodies uniformly distributed in a sphere with zero initial velocity. Simulate gravitational collapse and subsequent dynamics for 2000 timesteps. Produce figures/collapse_sequence.png (4-panel time series at t=0, t=500, t=1000, t=2000). Measure and report the collapse timescale and compare against the analytical free-fall time (cite Binney & Tremaine or equivalent from sources.bib).

items.description: Barnes-Hut accuracy experiment: theta parameter sweep
items.acceptance_criteria: For N=200, sweep theta in {0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0, 1.5}. Measure force error (RMS relative to direct summation) and wall-clock time. Produce results/experiments/theta_sweep.csv and figures/theta_tradeoff.png showing accuracy-vs-speed trade-off curve. Identify optimal theta value for <1% force error.

items.description: Synthesize experimental results into findings document
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/findings.md (>2000 words) covering: (1) summary of all integrator comparisons with quantitative results, (2) Barnes-Hut vs direct scaling analysis, (3) physical validation results (solar system, collapse), (4) adaptive timestep findings, (5) collision handling evaluation. Must include inline references to at least 8 papers from sources.bib. Must reference specific figures from figures/ directory.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: use writer agent for synthesis, reviewer agent for quality check.

items.description: Generate final concept-tree summary
items.acceptance_criteria: Run concept_evolve walk to produce a complete traversal of the concept tree accumulated during the project. Output must exist in results/concept_evolve/tree/final_summary.md listing all explored concepts, which were adopted, which were discarded, and why. Must reference at least 3 cross-domain insights discovered during concept exploration.
items.notes: Forces final concept-tree traversal and documentation.

items.description: Update README with project overview and usage instructions
items.acceptance_criteria: README.md must contain: (1) project title and one-paragraph description, (2) installation/dependency instructions, (3) usage examples for running simulation with different integrators and N values, (4) description of directory structure (src/, results/, figures/, scenarios/, tests/), (5) summary of key findings with references to results/findings.md. Must be >500 words.

items.description: Final review: all tests pass and all artifacts exist
items.acceptance_criteria: Run full test suite (tests/test_physics.py) -- all tests pass. Verify existence of all required artifacts: sources.bib (>=15 entries), results/findings.md, results/baseline/, results/verlet/, results/leapfrog/, results/barneshut/, results/adaptive/, results/collisions/, results/experiments/, figures/ (>=5 figures), results/concept_evolve/tree/ (>=5 files). Produce a checklist in results/final_checklist.md with pass/fail for each item.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: reviewer agent performs final quality check across all deliverables.
